say: Land records are flat.
Cities... aren't.
Bhoo Aayaam.
The three-D property registry.
One flat. Three records. Three different answers.
And today, an officer reconciles them by hand.
So, drop in anything. Maps, deeds, tables, plans, LiDAR.
Every original is sealed, the moment it lands.
When the data is unfamiliar,
AI reads it, byte by byte,
and proposes how to split it, and what each field means.
Then code does the converting. Nothing is invented.
The file is split by meaning.
AI normalises the first chunks,
while a second worker learns from every checked result.
Then the model takes over. Faster.
And the city streams onto the map, while it's still uploading.
Search any building, and fly straight to it.
Every value cites its source.
Every building opens into its floors. And every flat gets its own three-D Ulpin.
Straight from the documents, floor by floor.
Where the plan and the survey disagree, you see it, in place.
One click, and it's a finding.
Below the parcel, too. Water, sewer, gas.
Draw a trench, and see what it crosses, before you dig.
Every flat gets a Property Card, that anyone can verify.
Same revision. Same hash chain.
Built for the officer.
Open to the citizen.
Identify.
Prove.
Govern.
Bhoo Aayaam.
Every floor. Every flat. One verifiable record.
